images.title: A linear pair makes 180
images.purpose: Show that angles a and b sit side by side on a straight line and together make 180 degrees.
images.composition: Two crossing lines in the centre, only the upper two angles highlighted; the sum line sits under the figure.
exact_structure: A horizontal straight line m (grey #6B7280) through a centre point, and a second line l whose upper arm rises to the right at 60 degrees above the right arm of m, so that the upper left angle is 120 degrees and the upper right angle is 60 degrees.
Upper left angle a is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) and labelled 120 degrees.
Upper right angle b is filled teal (#0072B2) and labelled 60 degrees.
The two lower angles are not filled and carry no number.
A thin curved bracket above the horizontal line spanning a and b together, labelled 180 degrees (a straight angle).
The equation line a + b = 180° sits below the figure.
rejection: a and b not adding to 180 degrees in the drawing
extra angle numbers on the lower angles
images.takeaway: Two angles side by side on a straight line add to 180 degrees.
images.description: Two crossing lines with the upper angles of 120 and 60 degrees highlighted and a bracket marking 180 degrees.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students see that a and b fill a straight line, so b is 180 minus a.

image_decisions.why: The highlighted linear pair is the one idea the method uses.
